core.title: Declare DTOs in the contracts location
core.given: A source file that the stack's role assignment places inside a feature's internal layer, and that is not in the contracts location
core.when: a type recognized as a DTO by the stack's DTO naming idiom is declared in or moved into it
core.then: Declare the DTO type in the contracts location (a module owned by neither side of the boundary), not inside a feature's internal layer.
prefer: Canonical placement: declare the DTO in the contracts location and import that shared boundary shape from both sides of the boundary.
During GREEN: reuse an existing contract type that already represents the payload.
During GREEN: add only the fields the current acceptance requires.
During GREEN: create a new DTO only for a genuinely distinct boundary shape.
avoid: Declaring the DTO inside a feature's internal layer as a temporary shortcut.
Moving unrelated internal types into the contracts location.
Another feature importing a DTO declared inside one feature's internal layer (a private type leak).
unless: Test files and vendored or generated trees are never scanned.
A file assigned to no layer role is outside these rules, not in violation.
core.why: A DTO belongs to the contract (owned by neither side), not to either side; declared inside one feature's layer it becomes a private type that other features import anyway, so the boundary runs through somebody's internals.
evidence: Every affected DTO declaration lives in the contracts location.
The stack's placement check reports no DTO-placement finding for any affected DTO declaration.
verification: The check flags a DTO declaration (a type recognized by the stack's DTO naming idiom) in a scanned source file that is assigned to a layer role and not in the contracts location.

The check scans every DTO declaration in scanned files, pre-existing ones included; coder guidance fires on an added-or-moved declaration (change) or on a reported finding, combined with the file-kind and role facts.
Strict disposition: the check fails on every finding; there is no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline. Severity is declared by the realization.
Test files and vendored or generated trees are never scanned; the exact exclusion list is one stack-wide list (profile roots.excluded), and its exact classification is owned by the stack's checker.
Imports of external packages resolve outside the project graph and are not layer-checked (import-resolution exception); this does not exempt a locally declared DTO.
A file carrying no layer role is outside these rules rather than in violation of them.

values: assigned to a feature's internal layer

fires: A coder adds a DTO type in a source file assigned to a feature's internal layer and outside the contracts location.
A coder moves an existing DTO declaration into a layer-assigned source file outside the contracts location.
The placement check reports an existing DTO declaration in a layer-assigned source file outside the contracts location (e.g. one another feature imports — a private type leak).
doesNotFire: A DTO declared in the contracts location.
A DTO declared in a test file or in a vendored or generated tree (never scanned).
A DTO in a file assigned to no layer role (outside the rules, not in violation).
A type not recognized as a DTO by the stack's DTO naming idiom.
An import of an external package (not layer-checked); this does not suppress a finding for a locally declared DTO.

profileRequirements.bunValue: the path's layer segment ('path has a layer segment'); a file with no layer segment is outside these rules, not in violation

profileRequirements.meaning: The location where boundary-contract shapes (DTOs) are declared: owned by neither side of the boundary, identified by a path segment or glob relative to the source root.
profileRequirements.bunValue: a path segment `contracts` (declare the DTO in `contracts/`)

profileRequirements.meaning: Name patterns by which a type is recognized as a DTO (a boundary shape).
How an import of an external package (outside the project graph) is recognised, so it can be excluded from layer checking.
Vendored and generated trees that the check never scans (one stack-wide list; test files are outside the source scan as well).
profileRequirements.bunValue: Test files and vendored/build directories are never scanned.

proposedKeys.meaning: Where boundary-contract shapes (DTOs) are declared: a location owned by neither side of the boundary, as a path segment or glob relative to the source root.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: The layout group covers wagon, feature, commons, plan, test and e2e placements but not the shared contracts location; roles.<role>.path cannot express it because 'contracts' is not one of the closed role params.

proposedKeys.meaning: Name patterns by which a type is recognized as a DTO (a boundary shape).
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: idiom.dto_mapper_naming covers functions that map between DTOs and entities, not the DTO type names themselves; no other key says how a DTO type is recognized.

bunOnly.reason: Stack scoping of the Bun realization; a neutral core carries no language fact. Each stack realization gates the core on its own toolchain facts (e.g. profile tooling.languages).
Detector and finding ids of this rule are realization details; the core names the check generically (a DTO-placement finding).

bunOnly.text: bun_clean_architecture_detector reports no dto-placement finding for any affected `*DTO` declaration.
bunOnly.reason: Names the Bun detector and its finding id; the core's evidence refers generically to the stack's placement check.

bunOnly.text: contracts_module: a path segment `contracts` — where a boundary shape belongs, since it is owned by neither side.
bunOnly.reason: The term id and the literal path segment are the Bun realization of the contracts location; the core refers to that location through the profile key layout.contracts_dir.

bunOnly.text: private_type_leak: a DTO declared inside one feature's layer that another feature imports anyway, running the boundary through somebody's internals.
bunOnly.reason: The term id is realization vocabulary; the neutral concept is already carried by the core's avoid[3] and why.

neutralityNotes: The obligation itself (DTOs are declared in a contracts location owned by neither side, never inside one feature's internal layer) is fully neutral. Four things could not be made neutral and were pushed out of the core text: (1) the concrete contracts location — proposed as profile key layout.contracts_dir, since 'contracts' is neither a closed role nor any existing layout key; (2) the `*DTO` type-name suffix — proposed as idiom.dto_naming, since idiom.dto_mapper_naming covers mappers, not DTO type names; (3) realization identifiers (detector bun_clean_architecture_detector, finding id dto-placement, term ids contracts_module/private_type_leak, the numeric severity 3) — bunOnly, with the check described generically in core verification; (4) stack scoping facts (language typescript/bun, bare npm specifiers) — bunOnly/profile (tooling.languages, idiom.external_import). 'Import' is used in the generic sense of one module depending on another; each realization binds it to its own module syntax. The during-GREEN phase guidance and the behavioral-acceptance proof were already neutral.
